back: The legal status of being a member of a country, which gives rights and privileges and places duties on the person.

front: What are the three ways of becoming a Zimbabwean citizen?
back: By birth (section 36), by descent (section 37) and by registration (section 38).

front: What is the difference between citizenship by birth and by descent?
back: By birth: born in Zimbabwe to a citizen parent (or a grandparent who is a citizen by birth or descent). By descent: born outside Zimbabwe to a citizen parent or grandparent.

front: Give two ways a person can qualify for citizenship by registration.
back: Marriage to a citizen for at least five years; lawful continuous residence for at least ten years (also adoption by a citizen).

front: From what age can a citizen obtain a national identity card?
Which office issues birth certificates, IDs and passports?

back: Loyalty to Zimbabwe; observing the Constitution; respecting the flag and anthem; defending the country (also obeying laws and paying taxes).

front: Why is a birth certificate important?
back: It proves name, birth and parents and is needed for school, public examinations and an identity card.

front: When can citizenship by registration be revoked?
back: In limited cases set out in the Constitution, for example if it was obtained by fraud or false information.
